correctness.rationale: For n≥4 and 2≤k≤n−2, the CTMC generator is the rank-one update L=I−S+(a e0−b ek)(e0−ek)^T. The cyclic adjugate identity yields F(s)=d^n−1+a(d^(n−1)−d^(k−1))+b(d^(n−1)−d^(n−k−1)), d=1+s, without division at roots. The simple zero eigenvalue gives H=c2/c1; binomial coefficients reduce to the stated exact two-rate rational function. Its nonnegative excess vanishes only for n=4,k=2, while direct differentiation proves fixed-budget orientation and both independent-rate reversal inequalities, including equality at thresholds. An independent SymPy matrix determinant/coefficient comparison passed 15 (n,k) pairs with n≤8. This finite check is corroboration; the cyclic identity proves all n.

value.rationale: A natural fixed-rate network-design problem has a complete nonmonotonic answer: adding a reciprocal chord worsens integrated Kemeny relaxation for n≥5, yet increasing one rate can improve an already damaged network. Orientation budget and sharp thresholds would be useful exact benchmarks distinct from a routine calculation.

limitations: Only unit-rate directed cycles, one nonadjacent reciprocal pair, and nonnegative added rates; no general mixing-time implication.
